# Company 101 — Healthcare Administrative Automation OS

**Company ID:** `company:future:101`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:101`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-101-v2.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Roadmap conformance:** EXHAUSTIVE 28-PASS / A–BZ MAPPED; saturation subject to portfolio reverse-map reconciliation  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no healthcare operations, patient contact, payer submissions, clinical decisions, billing submissions, protected-data processing, customer onboarding, deployment, spending or public launch.  
**First-class project requirement:** independent Command Center project button, independent progress percentage, independent project pages, Brain/Agent/service state, Needs Me, incidents, dependencies, approvals and lifecycle.

## Business identity

Purpose: automate major portions of healthcare administration and revenue-cycle operations while preserving professional, privacy, legal, payer, contractual and human-review boundaries.

Core problem: healthcare administration is fragmented across EHRs, practice-management systems, payer portals, clearinghouses, fax/email/document workflows and payer-specific rules. Staff repeatedly re-key information, verify eligibility, chase authorization, correct claims, manage denials, reconcile payments and interpret changing administrative requirements.

Value proposition: reduce administrative burden, shorten cycle time, improve submission completeness, surface reimbursement variance, preserve evidence/provenance and route high-impact or ambiguous decisions to authorized human reviewers rather than pretending administrative automation is clinical judgment.

Non-goal: this company is not an autonomous physician, diagnostician, prescriber, utilization-review clinician or legal substitute. Clinical decisions and other legally/professionally reserved judgments remain outside unattended automation.

## Complete product tree

Healthcare Admin Control Center; Eligibility & Benefits Verification; Coverage Discovery; Prior Authorization Intake; Electronic Prior Authorization; Authorization Rules Engine; Authorization Evidence Pack Builder; Authorization Status Monitor; Referral Administration; Referral Network Routing; Claim Preparation; Claim Scrubbing; Coding Support/Validation; Documentation Completeness Review; Charge Capture Support; Claim Submission Orchestration; Claim Status Tracking; Rejection Correction; Denial Classification; Denial Root-Cause Analytics; Denial Work Queues; Appeal Draft/Evidence Builder; Appeal Deadline Manager; Payment Posting; ERA/EOB Parsing; Contractual Adjustment Validation; Payment Variance Detection; Underpayment Detection; Reimbursement Benchmarking; A/R Follow-up; Payer Portal Automation; Payer Policy Monitor; Payer Rule Knowledge Base; Fee Schedule Intelligence; Patient Financial Administration; Patient Estimate Support; Financial Assistance Workflow Support; Statement/Payment-Plan Administration; Refund/Credit-Balance Workflow; Credentialing/Enrollment Integration; Revenue-Cycle Analytics; Operational Benchmarking; Audit/Evidence Vault; Healthcare Admin API; Embedded SDK; White-Label RCM Infrastructure; Multi-Entity Enterprise Console; Specialty Packs; Payer Packs; State/Jurisdiction Packs; Interoperability Gateway.

## Complete feature tree

Patient/member identity matching; provider/facility identity; payer/plan identification; effective dates; benefits/deductible/copay/coinsurance/out-of-pocket capture; service/procedure context; referral requirements; authorization requirement detection; authorization question/criteria extraction; required-document checklist; clinical-document reference without independent diagnosis; evidence provenance; payer submission status; deadlines; claim edits; coding-rule checks; modifier checks; bundling/edit checks where licensed/authorized; documentation completeness; diagnosis/procedure linkage validation support; claim lifecycle; rejection reason normalization; denial taxonomy; appeal evidence; payment/adjustment normalization; contract/rate expectation comparison; aging; follow-up cadence; portal-session state; communication history; audit log; confidence; human-review gate; source freshness; payer-rule version; effective date; supersession; data-retention state; consent/authorization state; tenant; role; security classification.

## Complete customer tree

Independent practices; physician groups; specialty practices; clinics; ambulatory surgery centers; hospitals; health systems; dental/vision where domain packs fit; behavioral-health administrative organizations without clinical-decision automation; laboratories; imaging centers; DME suppliers where lawful; home-health/hospice administrative teams; RCM companies; medical billing companies; coding-support organizations; management-service organizations; provider networks; payers for administrative workflows; healthcare software vendors; EHR/practice-management vendors; clearinghouses; revenue-cycle consultancies; authorized government/health administration programs where procurement and law permit.

## Complete vertical tree

Primary care; cardiology; orthopedics; gastroenterology; dermatology; oncology administration; radiology/imaging; pathology/labs; surgery; anesthesia; physical/occupational therapy; behavioral-health administration; pediatrics; women’s-health administration; dental; vision; DME; home health; hospice administration; urgent care; multi-specialty groups; hospital outpatient; inpatient revenue-cycle administration; ambulatory surgery; specialty pharmacy administrative interfaces where lawful; payer/provider operations. Each vertical requires a bounded specialty pack with terminology, common payer workflows, documentation patterns and evaluation sets.

## Specialized Brain capability tree

The Healthcare Administrative Brain must know and reason over payer policies, eligibility, benefits, authorization, referrals, claim lifecycles, coding structures, reimbursement, denials, appeals, documentation completeness, payment variance, contractual rules, payer portals, administrative standards, interoperability standards and changing rule provenance.

Required capabilities: KNOW payer/plan/provider/admin vocabulary; UNDERSTAND administrative context and evidence; CLASSIFY workflow, denial, rejection, document, payer and risk; REASON about missing requirements and next administrative actions; PLAN multi-step work; PREDICT likelihood of administrative rejection/denial only as decision support; FORECAST queue/aging/workload; OPTIMIZE sequencing and staff attention; RECOMMEND next actions with evidence; DECIDE only within narrow pre-authorized administrative rules; EXECUTE low-risk administrative steps through governed tools; VERIFY submitted/received/reconciled state; EXPLAIN source/rule/rationale; ESCALATE uncertainty, high-impact exceptions and protected decisions.

The Brain must maintain strict distinction among: administrative fact; payer rule; source statement; inferred recommendation; clinician-authored content; human-approved decision. It must never silently convert an inference into a clinical fact.

## Brain architecture

Brain Factory base + healthcare administration domain pack + payer-policy retrieval layer + versioned rule/effective-date graph + specialty packs + workflow planner + confidence/evidence engine + deterministic validation services + human-review policy layer.

Memory: tenant-isolated operational memory; no cross-customer PHI learning by default; provenance-bound policy memory; expiry/freshness for payer rules; configurable retention; redaction/tokenization where appropriate.

Evaluations: authorization requirement detection; eligibility interpretation; claim-edit precision/recall; denial classification; payment variance accuracy; document-completeness accuracy; hallucination/source-faithfulness; stale-policy detection; PHI leakage; role/permission enforcement; high-impact decision refusal/escalation; portal-tool reliability; idempotency; duplicate-submission prevention.

## Complete Agent tree

Eligibility Agent; Benefits Verification Agent; Authorization Intake Agent; Authorization Evidence Agent; Authorization Status Agent; Referral Agent; Coding-Support Agent; Documentation Completeness Agent; Claim Preparation Agent; Claim Scrub Agent; Submission Agent; Rejection Agent; Claim Status Agent; Denial Triage Agent; Appeal Support Agent; Payment Posting Agent; Payment Variance Agent; Underpayment Agent; A/R Follow-up Agent; Payer Policy Monitor Agent; Portal Automation Agent; Patient-Financial-Administration Agent; RCM Analytics Agent; Integration Agent; Data Quality Agent; Security/Privacy Agent; Compliance Agent; Independent QA Agent; Incident/Reconciliation Agent.

Agents receive least-privilege scopes. High-impact actions, legal attestations, payer representations, clinical interpretations and protected external submissions require the appropriate authorization gate.

## Deterministic / non-agent services

FHIR/HL7 parsing; X12 transaction parsing/generation where appropriate; eligibility response normalization; ERA/EOB normalization; claim-schema validation; coding/table lookups under proper licensing; rule engines; deadline calculators; fee-schedule/rate tables; contract term evaluators; payment reconciliation; duplicate detection; patient/member/provider matching; document hashing; OCR/document extraction when authorized; redaction/tokenization; audit logging; idempotency keys; retry/dead-letter queues; portal session/replay state; consent/authorization state; encryption/key management; retention/deletion engine; metrics/tracing.

## Input tree

Patient/member demographics; insurance cards/plan identifiers; provider/facility data; appointment/service data; orders/referrals; clinician-authored notes/documents; authorization forms; payer policies; payer responses; claims; claim edits; clearinghouse acknowledgments; remittances; EOB/ERA; contracts/fee schedules; denial letters; appeal responses; correspondence; portal statuses; call notes; timestamps; billing ledgers; payment data; workflow rules; user approvals.

## Output tree

Eligibility/benefit summaries; authorization requirement findings; required-document checklists; submission-ready administrative packets; status alerts; claim-quality findings; corrected administrative claim candidates; denial reason classification; appeal draft/evidence pack; payment-posting candidates; variance/underpayment findings; A/R work queues; payer-policy change alerts; operational metrics; audit evidence; reconciliation reports; human-review tasks; API responses; exportable records.

## Workflow tree

Authorize tenant/workflow → identify patient/provider/payer/service → verify coverage/benefits → determine referral/authorization requirements → collect required evidence → human/professional review where necessary → submit through approved channel → monitor status → update scheduling/revenue-cycle state → prepare/scrub claim → submit → track acknowledgments/status → normalize rejection/denial → correct or assemble appeal support → monitor adjudication → ingest remittance → post/reconcile → detect variance/underpayment → follow up → close with evidence → retain/delete under policy.

## Integration tree

EHR; practice management; scheduling; billing; clearinghouses; payer APIs; payer portals; FHIR endpoints; HL7 interfaces; X12 gateways; document management; secure fax/messaging; SFTP; identity/SSO; credentialing systems; payment systems; data warehouses; BI; support/ticketing; call-center systems where authorized; audit/SIEM; cloud/object storage; notification providers.

## API / developer ecosystem

Eligibility API; benefits API; authorization-requirement API; authorization workflow API; claim-quality API; denial-classification API; payment-variance API; payer-policy API; status/webhook API; evidence/provenance API; administrative workflow SDK; sandbox/test fixtures; versioned schemas; webhook replay/idempotency; tenant-scoped keys; enterprise private-connect patterns.

## Data architecture

Tenant-isolated patient/member/provider/payer/workflow records; normalized administrative event model; payer/plan graph; policy/rule graph with source/effective dates; claim/authorization/payment lifecycle events; immutable audit/evidence ledger; document references; role/consent/authorization records; feature/quality metrics; encrypted secrets separated from business data; configurable region/residency; backup/recovery; legal-retention controls.

## Data moat

Potential moat comes from de-identified/authorized aggregate operational patterns, payer-rule normalization, workflow outcome evidence, denial/rejection taxonomies, integration reliability patterns, specialty administrative packs and verified rule-to-outcome relationships. No moat may depend on unauthorized exploitation of PHI, cross-tenant private data or prohibited secondary use.

## IP

Versioned payer-rule normalization system; administrative event ontology; evidence/provenance model; specialty workflow packs; interoperability adapters; denial/appeal taxonomy; payment-variance engine; portal reliability layer; evaluation corpus; deterministic guardrails; human-review policy engine.

## Monetization

Subscription by organization/site/provider; usage by eligibility/authorization/claim/denial/payment workflow; modular product pricing; enterprise license; API usage; private deployment; white-label/OEM; managed administrative automation; specialty/payer packs; outcome-linked administrative recovery pricing only where lawful and contractually appropriate. No revenue promise.

## Packaging

Starter eligibility/benefits; authorization suite; claims quality suite; denial/appeals suite; payment/reconciliation suite; full RCM administrative OS; enterprise multi-entity; API-only; embedded OEM; private/regulated deployment; specialty editions.

## Distribution

Healthcare software partnerships; RCM/billing partners; EHR/practice-management ecosystems; clearinghouse relationships; specialty associations; enterprise health-system procurement; implementation partners; channel/OEM. No outreach is authorized by this roadmap.

## Acquisition automation

Future low-risk automation may qualify inbound leads, map requested workflows to product modules, generate non-binding technical fit assessments and prepare demos/sandboxes. It must not send marketing, sign agreements, quote binding terms or represent compliance without authorization.

## Customer lifecycle

Discover → security/compliance review → integration assessment → sandbox/pilot → workflow validation → human-review calibration → controlled rollout → adoption monitoring → QA → expansion → renewal → export/transition/termination.

## Support / customer success

Healthcare-aware support with incident severity, integration diagnostics, rule/source explanation, payer-workflow troubleshooting, audit evidence, release notes, change-impact alerts, customer-specific configuration validation and training. Customer success tracks automation rate, cycle time, error/denial reduction and staff burden without claiming clinical outcomes unless validated and appropriate.

## Automation maximum / human-intervention minimum

Automate deterministic parsing, data normalization, eligibility queries, status polling, document completeness, rule lookup, deadline tracking, claim edits, routine work-queue routing, reconciliation and low-risk portal steps. Minimize manual re-keying and repetitive status chasing.

Human/professional intervention remains for ambiguous/high-impact clinical context, attestations, medical-necessity judgments, legal/compliance interpretations, unusual payer disputes, major financial exceptions, sensitive patient communications, contract interpretation beyond encoded terms and protected external commitments.

## Operations / administration

Tenant provisioning; integration onboarding; credential/connection lifecycle; policy/rule ingestion; release management; queue monitoring; payer portal health; support; billing; vendor management; data-retention administration; audit requests; incident handling; change management; backup/recovery; customer offboarding/export.

## Security

High-sensitivity architecture: encryption in transit/at rest; least privilege; strong tenant isolation; SSO/MFA; role/attribute-based access; secrets vault; just-in-time access; audited privileged actions; network restrictions; secure integration gateway; malware/file scanning; DLP; prompt-injection defenses for untrusted documents; model/tool egress controls; redaction; key rotation; vulnerability management; signed artifacts; security logging; incident response; vendor-risk assessment.

## Privacy

PHI/PII minimization; purpose limitation; configurable retention; patient/member matching controls; consent/authorization representation; access accounting; data export/deletion where applicable; region/residency controls; de-identification when appropriate; no training on customer PHI by default; privacy impact assessment; subprocessor inventory; breach/incident procedures.

## Compliance

Design for HIPAA/HITECH obligations where applicable, payer/clearinghouse contractual rules, healthcare transaction standards, state privacy/health-data requirements, records obligations, security frameworks and customer-specific controls. Compliance claims require actual validated controls and legal/compliance review; roadmap labels do not create certification.

## Legal

BAA/contract requirements, data-use limitations, payer portal terms, coding/content licenses, clearinghouse agreements, records retention, intellectual property, professional-practice boundaries, indemnity/liability, audit rights, subcontractor terms and jurisdiction-specific restrictions must be modeled. No agreement is signed by roadmap work.

## Abuse / misuse

Prevent fraudulent claims, fabricated documentation, unauthorized code changes, upcoding assistance, identity misuse, improper access to patient records, duplicate submission, unauthorized benefit queries, portal abuse, denial manipulation and extraction of restricted payer/customer data. Detect suspicious patterns and route to authorized review.

## Reliability

Idempotent submissions; durable queues; retries/backoff; dead-letter handling; transaction state machines; exactly-once-effect design where external semantics permit; portal/API failover strategies; source freshness; reconciliation; duplicate protection; degraded safe mode; manual fallback; backup/restore; disaster recovery; time-zone/deadline correctness.

## Observability

Per-tenant and per-workflow metrics: query/submission success; latency; queue age; portal/API health; authorization cycle time; claim rejection/denial categories; payment variance; automation rate; manual-review rate; model confidence; rule freshness; error rate; security events; cost per workflow; incident state. Trace every external action to source, actor, version and approval.

## Incident response

Severity model for PHI exposure, unauthorized access, wrong-patient matching, duplicate/incorrect submission, payer portal credential compromise, stale-rule use, payment posting errors, widespread integration outage and model/tool failures. Containment, suspend affected automation, preserve evidence, reconcile impacted records, notify authorized stakeholders, restore from known-good state, postmortem and control update.

## Testing

Unit; schema; integration; contract; sandbox payer/clearinghouse; portal replay; synthetic/de-identified fixtures; golden workflow; regression; security; privacy; permission; adversarial document/prompt; idempotency; duplicate-submission; disaster recovery; load/performance; data reconciliation; human-review calibration.

## Brain evaluations

Source faithfulness; payer-rule freshness; eligibility interpretation; authorization requirement recall/precision; documentation completeness; denial classification; payment variance; unsupported inference rate; escalation correctness; PHI leakage; cross-tenant leakage; prompt injection resistance; action authorization; tool-use reliability; explanation/provenance completeness.

## Deployment

Isolated dev/test/staging/production; regulated-data separation; region controls; infrastructure as code; signed releases; change approvals; canary/feature flags; rollback; schema migration gates; secret rotation; environment-specific integrations; customer pilot rings. No production deployment is authorized now.

## Scale

Prototype with synthetic/de-identified data → first controlled administrative workflow → specialty practice → multi-site group → RCM partner → health-system/enterprise scale → multi-payer/multi-region platform. Scale queue partitioning, rule freshness, integration pools, audit storage, model routing and support independently.

## Performance

Latency budgets vary by use: interactive eligibility/status seconds; batch claim/payment work minutes; policy ingestion asynchronous. Avoid blocking patient scheduling or billing operations on fragile AI calls; cache only within correctness/freshness bounds; use deterministic fast paths for known rules.

## Cost

Major drivers: model inference, document extraction, portal/browser automation, transaction fees, clearinghouse/payer connectivity, data storage, audit retention, support/security/compliance. Track per-workflow cost, vendor cost, model route, retry waste and internalization candidates. $0/free-first applies to Command Center build work; future commercial infrastructure requires authorization.

## Financial metrics

ARR/MRR if later real; gross/contribution margin; cost per eligibility/authorization/claim/denial/payment workflow; recovered underpayment where contractually measured; implementation cost; support cost; retention; expansion; automation rate; days in A/R; denial/rejection rate; cycle time. Never treat test data as revenue.

## Moat

Payer-rule/effective-date graph; specialty packs; normalized administrative event model; verified workflow outcomes; integration reliability; audit/provenance; evaluation corpus; enterprise trust; accumulated compatibility knowledge.

## Network effects

Possible non-private effects: broader payer-rule coverage, more integration adapters, better de-identified benchmark ranges, improved denial taxonomy and workflow reliability. Never require pooling identifiable patient/customer data.

## Platform

Can evolve from point solutions into a healthcare administrative operating layer coordinating data, policies, workflows, agents, deterministic services, audit evidence and third-party applications.

## White label / OEM

EHRs, practice-management vendors, RCM firms, clearinghouses and healthcare platforms may embed scoped modules through APIs/SDKs. Tenant ownership, branding, support, audit, model behavior and responsibility boundaries must remain explicit.

## Internationalization

Country-specific healthcare systems, payer models, coding/transaction standards, privacy rules, languages, currencies and reimbursement structures require separate domain packs. Do not assume US payer logic generalizes globally.

## Accessibility

WCAG-aligned admin interfaces; keyboard operation; screen-reader semantics; high-contrast/text scaling; accessible forms/tables/statuses; non-color-only alerts; understandable error explanations; accessible training/support materials.

## Mobile

Mobile is appropriate for status review, approvals, alerts, document capture where secure, and limited work queues; avoid forcing dense revenue-cycle work into phone-only UX. Strong device/session controls and remote logout required.

## Voice

Voice can support authenticated call summarization, payer-call notes and hands-free status queries only with consent, recording-law compliance and strong identity controls. Never fabricate payer statements; preserve transcript/source evidence.

## Multimodal

Documents, scans, cards, forms, EOBs, letters, portal screenshots and voice transcripts may be inputs. Extraction must preserve source regions/confidence and route ambiguity to review.

## Marketplace

Potential future marketplace for verified specialty packs, payer connectors, workflow templates and integration modules. No unreviewed third-party module receives patient-data/tool permissions by default.

## Developer ecosystem

Versioned APIs/SDKs; test sandboxes; synthetic fixtures; connector certification; schema registry; webhook contracts; developer portal; scoped credentials; sample apps; integration QA; deprecation policy.

## Partners

EHR/PMS vendors; clearinghouses; RCM companies; interoperability firms; security/compliance vendors; specialty consultants; implementation partners. Partnerships are architecture possibilities only, not authorized outreach.

## Training / certification

Role-based operator training; administrator training; integration certification; workflow pack certification; human-review calibration; security/privacy training; release/change training. Certification branding requires actual program definition later.

## Community

Future customer/operator community can share non-sensitive workflow practices, integration lessons and feature requests under moderation and confidentiality controls. No patient/customer data sharing.

## Content / knowledge

Versioned payer/admin knowledge library; source links; effective dates; specialty playbooks; integration runbooks; release notes; troubleshooting; policy change summaries; audit documentation; developer docs.

## Experimentation

Offline/sandbox evaluation first; synthetic/de-identified data where possible; shadow mode; A/B only where ethically/contractually appropriate; no silent experimentation on protected submissions or high-impact workflows; pre-defined success/safety metrics; rollback.

## Continuous improvement

Learn from incidents, manual overrides, denials/rejections, integration failures, customer configuration and rule changes. Update evaluation sets and compatibility profiles. Self-improvement remains governed: no uncontrolled model/prompt/rule promotion to production.

## Spinoffs

Potential modules/spinoffs: payer-policy intelligence, prior-auth infrastructure, denial intelligence, payment variance, healthcare portal automation, healthcare admin interoperability. Do not split merely to increase company count; classify against the new-company test.

## Cross-sell

Potential overlap with credentialing, document workflow, compliance, data quality, payment reconciliation, privacy/DSAR, security and workflow automation companies. Cross-sell may exist later but companies remain distinct.

## Bundling

Eligibility + authorization; claims + denial; payment + underpayment; full RCM admin suite; enterprise integration/security bundle; specialty editions. Bundling does not merge project identities.

## Failures

Wrong patient/member match; stale payer rule; missing authorization requirement; duplicate submission; incomplete evidence; wrong portal state; claim edit false positive/negative; denied appeal due deadline; payment mispost; integration timeout; credential expiry; rate limit; payer outage; model hallucination; document OCR error; cross-tenant leak; unauthorized action; rollback/reconciliation failure.

## Edge cases

Multiple coverages; retroactive eligibility; plan changes; coordination of benefits; emergency/exception workflows; secondary/tertiary claims; corrected/void claims; partial authorization; peer-to-peer requirement; payer portal unavailable; paper/fax-only workflows; conflicting policy sources; ambiguous EOB; capitation/value-based arrangements; provider enrollment gaps; mergers/TIN changes; unusual specialty rules; split billing; patient identity duplicates.

## Kill / safe mode

Per-tenant, per-integration, per-agent and per-workflow kill switches; read-only mode; stop external submissions while preserving status retrieval; force human review; disable model generation while deterministic services continue; revoke credentials; quarantine documents; rollback rule/model version; pause affected payer.

## Exit / portability

Export normalized administrative records, audit/evidence, configuration, policy/rule history, workflow state and customer-owned documents in documented formats; revoke integrations; delete/retain under contract/law; ensure customer can continue operations outside platform.

## Scale vision

Prototype → one administrative workflow → specialty-practice OS → multi-site provider groups → RCM infrastructure → enterprise health-system administrative platform → embedded infrastructure used by other healthcare software. Revenue-scale scenarios may be modeled but never promised.

## Autonomous mature state

Most repetitive administrative data movement, rule lookup, status monitoring, queue prioritization, reconciliation and document assembly run automatically. Brain/agents continually verify evidence and confidence. Humans focus on exceptions, professional judgment, high-impact disputes, policy/legal decisions and protected commitments. Every external action remains traceable, reversible where possible and bounded by authorization.

## Command Center dependencies

First-class Project Registry/button/detail/progress; Brain Factory; Agent Factory; Capability Registry; Proven Capability Profiles; Integration Registry; Identity/Tenant; Data Governance; Security/Privacy/Authorization Governors; Resource/Financial Governors; Testing/Evaluation Factory; Deployment/Recovery; Observability/Incident; Document intelligence; browser/portal workers; secrets/credential management; audit/provenance; versioning; approval/Needs Me.

## Retrofit risk

If Command Center lacks dynamic project identity, regulated-data isolation, per-company Brain/Agent scopes, versioned capability contracts, provenance, human-review gates, integration health, external-action idempotency and durable audit before this company exists, retrofitting healthcare-grade boundaries later would be expensive and unsafe.

## Phased roadmap

Phase 0 architecture/evaluation only → Phase 1 synthetic/de-identified eligibility/benefit normalization → Phase 2 controlled authorization/document workflows → Phase 3 claim quality/status → Phase 4 denial/appeal support → Phase 5 payment reconciliation/variance → Phase 6 multi-module RCM admin OS → Phase 7 enterprise/embedded/private deployment → Phase 8 continuous governed optimization/internalization.

Each phase requires explicit authorization before real customer/protected-data/production use.

## Reuse candidates

Project/tenant identity; audit/provenance; document extraction; workflow engine; human-review/approval; browser automation; integration adapters; queues; notifications; policy/version graphs; rule engine; redaction/tokenization; observability; incident/recovery; evaluation harness; billing/entitlement when later proven.

## Proven capability dependencies

No shared capability is automatically trusted merely because another company uses it. Critical shared infrastructure must reach the required proof maturity, pass healthcare-specific compatibility/security/privacy evaluations and preserve rollback/fork options before adoption.

## Company-specific capabilities

Healthcare administrative ontology; payer/plan/policy graph; FHIR/HL7/X12 healthcare adapters; authorization/claim/denial/payment domain logic; specialty packs; regulated-data controls; healthcare-specific evaluation suites; payer-portal behaviors.

## External dependencies to internalize

Repeated dependency candidates: document/OCR, browser automation, policy monitoring, workflow/rule engine, data validation, redaction/tokenization, integration reliability and model routing. Clearinghouses, payer networks and licensed coding/content sources may remain external where economics/legal access make internalization impractical.

## Blast-radius requirements

Critical: wrong-patient/cross-tenant access, mass incorrect submission, credential compromise, stale rule applied broadly, payment posting corruption, PHI leak. High-blast shared services require isolation, canaries, per-tenant limits, reconciliation, rollback and multi-company proof before standardization.

## Version / compatibility requirements

Version every API/schema, payer rule, specialty pack, Brain, agent policy, deterministic rule set, integration adapter and workflow. Track effective dates and customer configuration. Candidate releases require contract/regression/security/privacy/performance evaluation, staged rollout, migration plan and rollback.

# Exhaustive 28-pass findings

1. **Core Business:** coherent healthcare-administration OS; excludes clinical practice automation.
2. **Product Expansion:** point modules expand into full administrative/RMC infrastructure and embedded APIs.
3. **Customer Expansion:** provider, RCM, payer and software-vendor customers without collapsing different responsibility models.
4. **Industry / Vertical Expansion:** specialty packs required; no assumption one workflow fits all medicine.
5. **Specialized Brain:** full healthcare-administration domain Brain justified.
6. **Agent Decomposition:** specialized least-privilege agents mapped for each lifecycle segment.
7. **Deterministic Services:** transaction parsing, rule validation, reconciliation and identity matching must remain deterministic where possible.
8. **Data Products:** de-identified benchmark/rule intelligence possible only under authorization and privacy constraints.
9. **API / Developer Products:** modular APIs/SDKs are first-class product family.
10. **White Label / OEM / Embedded:** strong fit for EHR/PMS/RCM/clearinghouse embedding.
11. **Enterprise:** multi-entity, SSO, private connectivity, audit, residency and governance required.
12. **Marketplace / Platform:** connector/workflow-pack marketplace possible later with strict certification.
13. **Monetization:** subscription, usage, enterprise, API, OEM, managed modules; no revenue promise.
14. **Distribution:** partnerships/ecosystems/procurement; outreach remains unauthorized.
15. **Automation:** repetitive administrative steps highly automatable with evidence and idempotency.
16. **Human-Intervention Elimination:** remove re-keying/status chasing, not professional/legal judgment.
17. **Moats:** policy graph, specialty packs, verified outcomes, integration reliability, evaluation corpus.
18. **Security:** regulated/high-sensitivity controls are core architecture, not add-ons.
19. **Privacy:** PHI/PII minimization and tenant isolation mandatory.
20. **Compliance:** healthcare/admin/transaction/privacy obligations require versioned compliance packs and actual validation before claims.
21. **Failure / Edge Cases:** patient identity, payer state, duplicates, stale rules and partial external effects dominate failure design.
22. **Internationalization:** separate country healthcare/payer packs required.
23. **Scale:** shard by tenant/payer/workflow; preserve per-company and per-customer isolation.
24. **Future Technology:** improved interoperability, confidential computing, local/private models and better structured payer APIs may reduce friction.
25. **Cross-Company Synergy:** substantial reusable infrastructure, but no shared private healthcare data.
26. **Spinoffs:** several modules could later qualify; no automatic split.
27. **Adversarial Missing-Idea Pass:** added coordination-of-benefits, patient financial admin, specialty packs, portal safe mode, rule effective dates, regulated evaluation, portability and provider/payer responsibility separation.
28. **Saturation Pass:** remaining material branches are captured as specialty/payer/country packs, integrations, shared-capability candidates or explicit adjacent-company overlaps; no new top-level branch currently justifies changing Company 101 identity.

workUnits.title: Reconcile and implement Business identity
acceptanceCriteria:
Original section Business identity (source line 11):
Purpose: automate major portions of healthcare administration and revenue-cycle operations while preserving professional, privacy, legal, payer, contractual and human-review boundaries.

Core problem: healthcare administration is fragmented across EHRs, practice-management systems, payer portals, clearinghouses, fax/email/document workflows and payer-specific rules. Staff repeatedly re-key information, verify eligibility, chase authorization, correct claims, manage denials, reconcile payments and interpret changing administrative requirements.

Value proposition: reduce administrative burden, shorten cycle time, improve submission completeness, surface reimbursement variance, preserve evidence/provenance and route high-impact or ambiguous decisions to authorized human reviewers rather than pretending administrative automation is clinical judgment.

Non-goal: this company is not an autonomous physician, diagnostician, prescriber, utilization-review clinician or legal substitute. Clinical decisions and other legally/professionally reserved judgments remain outside unattended automation.

# Company 102 — E-Discovery & Litigation Evidence Intelligence Platform

**Company ID:** `company:future:102`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:102`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-102-v2.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Roadmap conformance:** EXHAUSTIVE 28-PASS / A–BZ MAPPED; saturation subject to portfolio reverse-map reconciliation  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no client matter ingestion, legal hold, discovery production, court filing, privilege determination, legal advice, outreach, spending, deployment or public launch.  
**First-class project requirement:** independent Command Center project button, percentage, project pages, Brain/Agent/service state, evidence/checkpoints, Needs Me, incidents, approvals, dependencies and lifecycle.

## Business identity

Purpose: help authorized legal teams ingest, preserve, organize, search, analyze, understand, review and verify large bodies of litigation and investigation evidence while preserving chain of custody, privilege boundaries, confidentiality, legal-hold requirements and human attorney judgment.

Core problem: litigation evidence spans email, messaging, documents, spreadsheets, databases, images, audio, video, logs, testimony and third-party productions. Manual review is expensive and error-prone, while AI-only review is unsafe if provenance, privilege, completeness, explainability and review controls are weak.

Value proposition: evidence-centered intelligence that accelerates review, chronology, entity/communication analysis, issue spotting, contradiction/corroboration detection, exhibit preparation and production workflows without pretending to replace counsel or making unreviewed legal conclusions.

Non-goal: not a generic “AI lawyer,” not autonomous legal advice, not an unattended privilege-waiver engine, not a system for fabricating evidence or altering source material.

## Complete product tree

Matter Intake; Legal Hold Coordination; Custodian Registry; Evidence Collection Orchestration; Source Connector Library; Forensic Metadata Capture; Chain-of-Custody Ledger; Hash/Integrity Verification; Ingestion & Normalization; Deduplication; Near-Deduplication; Email Threading; Family/Attachment Grouping; OCR/Transcription; Language Detection/Translation Support; Search; Semantic Search; Concept Clustering; Relevance Ranking; Technology-Assisted Review Support; Issue Tagging; Entity Extraction; Entity Resolution; Communication Graph; Relationship Graph; Chronology Builder; Event Reconstruction; Contradiction Detection; Corroboration Detection; Testimony Comparison; Claim/Defense Evidence Mapping; Privilege-Indicator Screening; Confidentiality/Designation Support; PII/Sensitive Data Detection; Redaction Workflow; Review Workspace; Review QA; Sampling/Validation; Production Set Builder; Bates/Numbering Support; Export/Load Files; Exhibit Builder; Deposition Prep; Witness/Topic Dossiers; Discovery Request/Response Mapping; Evidence Citation Generator; Audit/Evidence Vault; Case Analytics; API/SDK; Enterprise Private Deployment; Managed Review Infrastructure; Government/Investigation Edition; Cross-Border Discovery Pack.

## Complete feature tree

Matter/case IDs; custodian; source; collection method; timestamps; hashes; original/native/derived relationships; message/thread/family links; document versions; extracted text; OCR confidence; transcript timestamps; entities; aliases; relationships; topics; issue tags; relevance labels; reviewer decisions; reviewer confidence; privilege indicators; redaction regions; confidentiality designations; production status; Bates IDs; deposition/exhibit links; timeline events; contradictions/corroborations; evidence citations; search queries; saved views; hold state; retention state; audit history; export history; model/version provenance; review overrides; sampling metrics.

## Complete customer tree

Law firms; litigation boutiques; corporate legal departments; in-house investigations; e-discovery service providers; litigation support vendors; authorized government legal/investigative teams; insurers handling litigation; regulated enterprises with complex investigations; expert teams where authorized; compliance/investigations departments. Separate responsibility and privilege models are required per customer type.

## Complete vertical tree

Commercial litigation; employment matters; product liability; intellectual property disputes; antitrust/competition matters; regulatory investigations; internal investigations; securities/financial litigation; insurance litigation; construction disputes; healthcare administration disputes; government investigations; class-action/mass-tort support; arbitration; cross-border disputes; white-collar investigations. Domain packs must not become legal-advice models.

## Specialized Brain capability tree

The Litigation Evidence Brain must KNOW evidence structures, document families, communication patterns, chronology, discovery workflows, review taxonomies, privilege indicators, production concepts and matter-specific issue definitions. It must UNDERSTAND evidence relationships and provenance; CLASSIFY documents/issues/relevance/privilege indicators with uncertainty; REASON about chronology, actors, contradictions and corroboration; PLAN review/deposition/exhibit preparation; PREDICT review prioritization as assistive analytics; OPTIMIZE review order and sampling; RECOMMEND evidence links and questions; VERIFY claims against cited sources; EXPLAIN every finding with evidence; ESCALATE privilege/high-impact/ambiguous matters.

The Brain must never silently assert that an allegation is true. It must distinguish source fact, party claim, model inference, reviewer conclusion, legal theory and unresolved conflict.

## Brain architecture

Brain Factory base + litigation/evidence domain pack + matter-specific issue pack + immutable evidence graph + retrieval layer + chronology engine + relationship graph + review feedback layer + deterministic integrity/provenance services + policy/privilege guardrail layer.

Memory is matter-isolated; no cross-client matter learning from private evidence by default. Privileged/confidential data boundaries are stricter than ordinary tenant boundaries. Every model output links to source evidence/version where feasible.

Brain evaluations: citation accuracy; chronology ordering; entity resolution; contradiction/corroboration precision; relevance ranking; privilege-indicator recall/precision; hallucination rate; source-faithfulness; cross-matter leakage; redaction accuracy; review consistency; prompt injection/document poisoning; evidence tamper detection; legal-conclusion refusal/escalation.

## Complete Agent tree

Matter Intake Agent; Collection Agent; Metadata Agent; Integrity/Hash Agent; OCR/Transcription Agent; Dedup/Threading Agent; Entity Agent; Chronology Agent; Communication Graph Agent; Relevance Triage Agent; Issue Tag Agent; Contradiction Agent; Corroboration Agent; Privilege-Indicator Agent; Redaction Agent; Review QA Agent; Sampling/Validation Agent; Discovery Mapping Agent; Production Agent; Exhibit Agent; Deposition Prep Agent; Provenance Agent; Security/Privacy Agent; Independent QA Agent.

Agents may suggest and prepare; privilege waiver, final production, final redaction approval, litigation strategy, filing and binding legal decisions require authorized human review.

## Deterministic / non-agent services

Cryptographic hashing; immutable object manifests; chain-of-custody ledger; file type detection; metadata parsers; archive expansion; OCR/transcription engines; exact/near duplicate detection; email threading; attachment family linking; text indexing; regex/query search; Bates/production numbering; export/load-file generation; redaction rendering; audit logging; legal-hold state machine; retention engine; permission enforcement; document virus/malware scanning; DLP; backup/restore; reproducible transformation pipelines.

## Input tree

Email/mailboxes; chat exports; SMS; collaboration messages; PDFs; Office docs; text; spreadsheets; presentations; images; audio; video; databases; structured exports; cloud drives; source-control logs where relevant; system logs; contracts; policies; testimony/transcripts; pleadings; discovery requests; productions; exhibits; custodial metadata; reviewer labels; issue definitions; legal-hold instructions.

## Output tree

Normalized evidence corpus; deduplicated/threaded views; searchable indexes; chronology; entity/relationship maps; communication graphs; issue/relevance queues; privilege-indicator queues; contradiction/corroboration findings; review sets; QA samples; redacted derivatives; production packages; load files; exhibit books; witness/topic dossiers; deposition-prep packets; evidence-linked summaries; audit/provenance reports; exportable matter records.

## Workflow tree

Authorize matter → define legal/privilege/security boundaries → register custodians/sources → issue/track hold where applicable → collect with provenance → hash/preserve originals → normalize/OCR/transcribe → deduplicate/thread/family-link → index/search/cluster → define issues/review protocol → prioritize/review → privilege/confidentiality/redaction review → QA/sample validation → map discovery requests → prepare production → human approval → export/produce through authorized process → build chronology/exhibits/deposition support → preserve audit/retention/termination evidence.

## Integration tree

Email/Google Workspace/Microsoft 365; collaboration platforms; cloud storage; enterprise file shares; e-discovery collection sources; litigation databases; document management; case-management systems; SSO/identity; secure transfer/SFTP; transcription/OCR; legal-hold systems; ticketing/work management; SIEM/audit; storage/object stores; search/vector/graph engines; court/e-filing references only where later authorized and appropriate.

## API / developer ecosystem

Collection API; evidence ingest API; metadata/provenance API; search API; entity/chronology API; review-label API; production/export API; redaction API; matter webhook API; connector SDK; custom parser SDK; sandbox synthetic matters; schema/version registry; audit/event API; private deployment interfaces.

## Data architecture

Matter-isolated evidence stores; immutable native evidence; derived-artifact store; metadata index; text/search index; entity/relationship graph; chronology graph; reviewer decision store; privilege/confidentiality partitions; production manifests; legal-hold state; audit ledger; access logs; retention schedules; encryption keys scoped by matter/customer where appropriate.

## Data moat

Potential moat: verified evidence-processing patterns, parser/connector coverage, entity-resolution quality, chronology/review evaluation corpus, de-identified workflow benchmarks, production reliability and matter-structure ontology. Never pool private client evidence or privileged material across matters to create a moat without explicit lawful authorization.

## IP

Evidence graph; chain-of-custody/provenance model; chronology reconstruction; matter issue/claim map; contradiction/corroboration engine; reviewer consistency/QA engine; production validation; secure evidence transformation pipeline; matter-isolated Brain architecture; evaluation framework.

## Monetization

Per matter; per GB/TB ingested/hosted; per document/review volume; reviewer seats; enterprise subscription; private deployment; API; managed infrastructure; collection/processing modules; advanced analytics; production/exhibit modules. No revenue promise.

## Packaging

Collection/processing; review/TAR support; chronology/intelligence; privilege/redaction; production; deposition/exhibit; investigations edition; enterprise private deployment; API/embedded; managed e-discovery infrastructure.

## Distribution

Legal-tech partnerships; e-discovery providers; law-firm procurement; enterprise legal operations; litigation-support firms; integrators; secure private deployment channels. No outreach is authorized by roadmap work.

## Acquisition automation

Future system may qualify inbound matters, estimate technical processing needs, identify required connectors and generate non-binding solution scopes. It may not solicit clients, establish attorney-client relationships, quote binding legal services or give legal advice without authorization.

## Customer lifecycle

Security/privilege review → matter scoping → data-source assessment → pilot/validation → collection/processing → review calibration → production support → matter closure → retention/export/deletion → postmatter performance review.

## Support / customer success

Matter-critical support; ingestion failures; parser issues; indexing/search; production validation; access/permission issues; performance; evidence integrity; export; incident response. Customer success measures review efficiency, precision/recall where validated, cycle time, production quality and platform adoption—not legal outcomes.

## Automation maximum / human-intervention minimum

Automate collection orchestration, hashing, normalization, dedup/threading, indexing, entity extraction, chronology candidates, clustering, review prioritization, redaction detection candidates, QA sampling and production validation.

Retain attorneys/authorized reviewers for privilege decisions, legal relevance standards, litigation strategy, final redactions, final production, legal assertions, filing and evidentiary judgment.

## Operations / administration

Matter provisioning; secure access; connector credentials; evidence transfer; storage tiers; hold/retention administration; reviewer role management; model/version control; support; billing; export/offboarding; incident handling; backup/recovery; vendor/subprocessor management; compliance audits.

## Security

Extremely high confidentiality: encryption; matter/customer isolation; SSO/MFA; least privilege; ethical wall/conflict-aware access; just-in-time privileged access; immutable logs; secure evidence upload; malware scanning; DLP; egress controls; secure model routing; no provider training on matter data by default; key rotation; signed artifacts; secure deletion; incident response; forensic audit.

## Privacy

PII/sensitive data minimization; special-category data handling; configurable jurisdiction/retention; data-subject obligations where applicable without compromising legal holds; redaction/tokenization; cross-border transfer controls; privacy by matter; no unauthorized secondary use.

## Compliance

Support customer obligations for legal hold, discovery process, records retention, privacy/security frameworks, court/agency production specifications and jurisdiction-specific requirements. Roadmap does not claim legal compliance certification; actual deployment requires counsel/customer validation.

## Legal

Attorney-client privilege; work product; confidentiality; protective orders; legal holds; evidence preservation; spoliation risk; discovery rules; data-processing agreements; cross-border discovery; subpoena/production requirements; licensing; retention; ethical walls; authorized practice boundaries. The platform assists legal teams and does not independently practice law.

## Abuse / misuse

Prevent evidence alteration, fabrication, concealment, spoliation, unauthorized deletion, privilege fishing across matters, improper surveillance, credential abuse, unauthorized collection, chain-of-custody tampering, deceptive redaction and prompt/document attacks intended to manipulate review.

## Reliability

Immutable originals; reproducible processing; idempotent ingestion; resumable large transfers; hash verification; checkpointed indexing; job queues; retry/dead-letter; search consistency; production validation; backup/restore; disaster recovery; no silent partial export; schema/version compatibility.

## Observability

Matter ingestion throughput; processing failures; parser coverage; index completeness; search latency; review queue age; duplicate rates; OCR/transcript confidence; reviewer disagreement; privilege/redaction QA; production validation; storage cost; model/tool cost; permission/security events; export integrity; incident state.

## Incident response

Critical incidents: cross-matter data exposure, lost/tampered evidence, improper deletion despite hold, privilege exposure, incorrect production package, corrupted native evidence, credential compromise. Immediate containment, preserve forensic evidence, suspend affected exports/actions, reconcile manifests/hashes, notify authorized legal/security owners, restore known-good state, document postmortem.

## Testing

Parser corpus; archive bombs/malware; metadata preservation; hash stability; dedup/threading; OCR/transcription; entity resolution; chronology; search; access/ethical-wall controls; cross-matter isolation; privilege/redaction evaluation; production manifest; load-file compatibility; export round-trip; backup/restore; load/performance; prompt injection/document poisoning; model source-faithfulness.

## Brain evaluations

Evidence citation correctness; no-source assertion rate; chronology accuracy; entity resolution; contradiction/corroboration precision; review ranking; privilege indicator quality; hallucination; cross-matter leakage; prompt injection resistance; legal-conclusion boundaries; explanation/provenance completeness; reviewer override learning governance.

## Deployment

Private/isolated environments; customer-region controls; optional single-tenant/private cloud/on-prem style architecture; dev/test/staging/production separation; signed releases; canary; migration gates; rollback; secure model/provider routing; customer-specific integration rings. No production deployment authorized now.

## Scale

Small matter → complex multi-custodian matter → enterprise litigation portfolio → major investigations → private legal-tech infrastructure. Scale object storage, search indexes, graph workloads, OCR/transcription, review queues and export pipelines independently while preserving matter isolation.

## Performance

Interactive search low latency; large ingestion/processing asynchronous; production jobs checkpointed; graph/semantic analytics batch-friendly. Prioritize deterministic evidence integrity over model speed.

## Cost

Storage/retention; indexing/search; OCR/transcription; model inference; transfer/egress; backup; private deployment; support/security/compliance. Track per-GB, per-document, per-matter and per-review-workflow cost; aggressively avoid duplicate processing.

## Financial metrics

ARR/MRR if later real; matter revenue; processing/hosting gross margin; cost per GB/document; support burden; reviewer-seat utilization; retention/expansion; storage margin; model cost percentage; implementation cost. No test revenue.

## Moat

Evidence/provenance trust; broad parser/connector support; matter graph; chronology/review quality; secure private architecture; production reliability; evaluation corpus; workflow knowledge.

## Network effects

Non-private effects from parser coverage, connector reliability, public-format compatibility and de-identified workflow benchmarks. No cross-client evidence pooling.

## Platform

Can become an evidence operating layer spanning collection, processing, review, intelligence, production and investigation support.

## White label / OEM

E-discovery providers, litigation-support firms and legal-tech platforms may embed processing/search/intelligence modules. Matter ownership, privilege, audit and customer identity remain explicit.

## Internationalization

Languages, scripts, date/time formats, local discovery rules, privacy/cross-border restrictions, data localization and court production formats require jurisdiction packs and counsel validation.

## Accessibility

Accessible review/search interfaces; keyboard-heavy review workflow; screen-reader semantics; scalable text; non-color-only issue labels; accessible media transcripts/captions; accessible export/reporting.

## Mobile

Mobile limited to secure review status, approvals, alerts and selected document review. High-risk export/production and dense evidence analysis favor desktop; device controls and remote session revocation required.

## Voice

Voice may assist searching, note dictation and deposition-prep queries in secure environments; recordings/transcripts require consent/privacy controls and source distinction.

## Multimodal

Documents, scans, photos, audio, video, spreadsheets, logs and metadata are native evidence types. Model outputs must point back to exact document/page/time/region where possible.

## Marketplace

Potential certified connector/parser/analytics-pack marketplace. Third-party code never receives unrestricted matter access; sandbox, signing, permission scopes and certification required.

## Developer ecosystem

Connector SDK; custom parser SDK; evidence schema; search/graph API; review API; production/export contracts; test corpus; versioning/deprecation; certification harness.

## Partners

Legal-tech vendors; e-discovery providers; forensic collection vendors; secure hosting providers; transcription/OCR providers; litigation consultants. Partnerships are planning only.

## Training / certification

Administrator, reviewer, production, security and connector training; review protocol calibration; evidence handling; privilege/redaction workflow; production validation; incident response.

## Community

Future professional community for non-confidential workflow practices, parser feedback and product ideas; no matter data or privileged content sharing.

## Content / knowledge

Product docs; evidence-format guides; connector docs; processing explanations; review playbooks; production validation; security/privilege guides; release/change notes; jurisdiction pack documentation.

## Experimentation

Synthetic/public benchmark corpora; shadow ranking; offline review evaluation; controlled A/B of review workflow only when permitted; no silent changes to legal-hold, privilege, production or source integrity.

## Continuous improvement

Learn from parser failures, reviewer disagreements, production validation issues and incident postmortems. Promote new models/rules only after evaluation, versioning and governed rollout.

## Spinoffs

Evidence graph API; chronology engine; redaction engine; secure review QA; production validator; forensic ingestion service. Keep as modules unless distinct buyer/value/roadmap passes new-company test.

## Cross-sell

Adjacent companies: data lineage/provenance, privacy redaction, legal/compliance monitoring, document workflow, identity/access review, backup integrity, content moderation. Cross-sell does not merge identities.

## Bundling

Collection + processing; review + intelligence; privilege + redaction; production; deposition/exhibit; full litigation evidence platform; private enterprise edition.

## Failures

Missing source; incomplete collection; broken archive; metadata loss; hash mismatch; duplicate misclassification; OCR error; entity collision; chronology error; privilege false negative; redaction leak; production omission; wrong matter access; corrupted export; model hallucination; prompt/document poisoning; retention deletion conflict.

## Edge cases

Encrypted/password files; unsupported proprietary formats; deleted/recovered artifacts; huge mailboxes; nested archives; foreign languages; handwritten scans; low-quality audio; conflicting timestamps/time zones; duplicate identities; forwarded messages; partial productions; mixed-privilege families; protective-order restrictions; cross-border data; rolling productions; late custodians.

## Kill / safe mode

Per matter, connector, model, agent and production kill switch; read-only evidence mode; disable exports/productions; quarantine suspect files; freeze deletion; revert model/rule version; revoke user/session/credential; preserve originals and audit.

## Exit / portability

Export natives, derivatives, metadata, hashes, audit trail, review decisions, issue tags, productions, load files, configuration and chain-of-custody manifests in documented formats; revoke credentials; retain/delete consistent with hold and contract.

## Scale vision

Single matter → multi-matter firm → enterprise legal department → investigation/e-discovery provider infrastructure → embedded evidence intelligence platform.

## Autonomous mature state

Collection, normalization, indexing, dedup/threading, metadata QA, relevance prioritization, chronology candidates, relationship mapping, QA sampling and production validation are highly automated. Attorneys/reviewers retain control over legal strategy, privilege, relevance standards, redactions, final production and evidentiary assertions.

## Command Center dependencies

First-class project identity/button/progress/pages; Brain Factory; Agent Factory; evidence/provenance capability; immutable storage patterns; Integration Registry; Identity/Tenant; Security/Privacy/Authorization Governors; Testing/Evaluation; Deployment/Recovery; Observability/Incident; document/multimodal intelligence; search/vector/graph; secrets; data-retention/legal-hold state; audit/versioning.

## Retrofit risk

If immutable evidence provenance, matter isolation, privileged-data boundaries, versioned model/evidence citations, large artifact pipelines and protected export/production gates are not designed early, this company cannot safely reuse generic shared infrastructure later.

## Phased roadmap

Phase 0 architecture + synthetic evidence corpus → Phase 1 ingest/hash/normalize/search → Phase 2 dedup/thread/entity/chronology → Phase 3 review prioritization/issue/QA → Phase 4 privilege/redaction support → Phase 5 production validation/export → Phase 6 deposition/exhibit intelligence → Phase 7 enterprise/private/OEM → Phase 8 governed continuous improvement.

## Reuse candidates

Identity/tenant; immutable audit/provenance; document/media extraction; search/vector/graph; workflow/queues; redaction/tokenization; access control; storage; observability; incident/recovery; evaluation harness; connectors; versioning.

## Proven capability dependencies

Generic components require legal/matter-specific fit testing. Critical evidence, identity, redaction, export and access services require sufficient proof maturity, security/privacy evaluation and rollback/fork options before broad sharing.

## Company-specific capabilities

Matter/evidence ontology; chain-of-custody model; legal-hold workflows; document families/threading; privilege-indicator policy; production/load-file tooling; litigation issue graph; chronology/testimony comparison; evidence citation semantics.

## External dependencies to internalize

Potential recurring candidates: OCR/transcription, document parsing, search/graph, redaction, secure file transfer, workflow orchestration and evaluation. Court/vendor-specific collection and licensed legal content may remain external.

## Blast-radius requirements

Critical: cross-matter exposure, evidence corruption/deletion, privilege exposure, mass wrong production/export, credential compromise. Enforce matter-scoped limits, immutable originals, export gates, canaries, reconciliation and rollback.

## Version / compatibility requirements

Version parsers, evidence schema, model, review taxonomy, issue packs, connector, production format, redaction engine and API. Preserve original source and reproducible derivation lineage across upgrades.

# Company 103 — KYC / KYB / AML Compliance Infrastructure

**Company ID:** `company:future:103`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:103`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-103-v2.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Roadmap conformance:** EXHAUSTIVE 28-PASS / A–BZ MAPPED; saturation subject to portfolio reverse-map reconciliation  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no identity verification, sanctions screening, account opening, transaction blocking, suspicious-activity filing, financial onboarding, customer contact, paid data purchase, deployment or public launch.  
**First-class project requirement:** independent Command Center project button, percentage, pages, Brain/Agent/service state, evidence/checkpoints, Needs Me, incidents, approvals, dependencies and lifecycle.

## Business identity

Purpose: provide identity, business verification, customer due diligence, risk, monitoring and regulated onboarding infrastructure for authorized financial and regulated digital businesses.

Core problem: KYC/KYB/AML workflows combine fragmented identity evidence, business registries, beneficial ownership, sanctions/PEP/watchlists, onboarding policies, risk models, case management, periodic reviews and transaction-monitoring inputs. Poorly designed automation either creates excessive manual review or takes unsafe high-impact actions without adequate evidence.

Value proposition: evidence-centered, configurable compliance infrastructure that separates deterministic screening and policy rules from probabilistic intelligence, keeps customer-specific policy explicit, preserves provenance and escalates consequential or ambiguous cases to authorized compliance personnel.

Non-goal: not autonomous legal/compliance counsel; not a system that independently opens/closes accounts, files regulatory reports, freezes funds or makes protected financial decisions without authorized governance.

## Complete product tree

KYC API; KYB API; Identity Verification Orchestrator; Document Verification; Address Verification; Age/Attribute Verification; Liveness/Biometric Integration Gateway where lawful; Device/Risk Signal Gateway; Business Registry Verification; Entity Status Monitor; Director/Officer Verification; Beneficial Ownership Graph; Parent/Subsidiary Graph; Industry/Business Activity Classification; Customer Due Diligence; Enhanced Due Diligence; Sanctions Screening; PEP Screening; Watchlist Screening; Adverse-Media Workflow Support; Risk Scoring Engine; Policy Rules Engine; Onboarding Decision Support; Manual Review Workbench; Evidence Vault; Case Management; Ongoing Identity/Business Monitoring; Periodic Review Scheduler; Customer Refresh; Transaction-Monitoring Integration; Alert Triage; Suspicious-Pattern Escalation; Regulatory/Policy Change Pack; Screening List Versioning; False-Positive Reduction; Matching/Name Resolution; Audit/Exam Pack; Consent/Disclosure Administration; Embedded SDK; White Label; Enterprise Multi-Jurisdiction Console; Private Deployment; Developer Sandbox.

## Complete feature tree

Person/entity identity; names/aliases; DOB/incorporation dates; addresses; documents; document authenticity signals; evidence source; business registration; entity status; directors; owners; ownership percentages; UBO thresholds; parent/subsidiary links; industry/activity; jurisdictions; citizenship/residency where lawful; watchlist/sanctions/PEP matches; match confidence; list/source/version/effective date; adverse-media references; risk factors; risk score; policy version; customer risk tier; review reason; reviewer decision; approval/escalation; periodic review date; monitoring trigger; case status; linked accounts/entities; transaction-monitoring alert references; audit trail; data retention; consent/legal basis where applicable.

## Complete customer tree

Banks; credit unions; fintech; lenders; payment processors; payment facilitators; marketplaces; broker/dealer-like regulated businesses where applicable; insurance; remittance providers; digital asset businesses where lawful; B2B SaaS with regulated onboarding obligations; gig/platform businesses; enterprise procurement/vendor onboarding teams with KYB needs; regulated ecommerce; compliance technology vendors; fraud/risk platforms.

## Complete vertical tree

Retail banking; business banking; lending; payments; merchant onboarding; marketplaces; insurance; remittance; wealth/financial services; digital assets where lawful; embedded finance; B2B vendor verification; platform seller verification; high-risk industry onboarding; cross-border financial services. Each vertical requires policy/jurisdiction packs and customer-specific risk appetite.

## Specialized Brain capability tree

The Compliance Intelligence Brain must KNOW identity/business structures, sanctions/PEP/watchlist concepts, ownership, risk factors, onboarding policies, periodic review, case workflows and jurisdictional differences. It must UNDERSTAND evidence quality and source freshness; CLASSIFY entities, industries, match types and risk factors; REASON about identity resolution, ownership chains, risk context and missing evidence; PLAN evidence collection/review; PREDICT only as assistive risk analytics; OPTIMIZE review queues/false-positive reduction; RECOMMEND actions with cited evidence; VERIFY source/version/policy; EXPLAIN each factor; ESCALATE protected/high-risk/ambiguous decisions.

It must distinguish factual source data, deterministic rule match, probabilistic identity match, model inference, customer policy and human compliance decision.

## Brain architecture

Brain Factory base + KYC/KYB/AML domain pack + jurisdiction/policy packs + entity/ownership graph + identity-resolution layer + source/provenance engine + deterministic screening/rules engine + risk-model layer + case context + human compliance review policy.

Memory is customer/tenant isolated. Screening sources, policies and risk models are versioned with effective dates. No customer-specific risk appetite silently leaks across tenants.

Evaluations: identity matching; entity resolution; ownership graph accuracy; sanctions/PEP match recall/precision; false-positive management; industry classification; source freshness; unsupported inference; adverse-media citation; policy execution; escalation; cross-tenant leakage; bias/fairness where applicable; document/prompt injection; audit explanation completeness.

## Complete Agent tree

Identity Intake Agent; Document Evidence Agent; Address/Attribute Agent; Business Registry Agent; Entity Resolution Agent; Ownership/UBO Agent; Sanctions Agent; PEP Agent; Watchlist Agent; Adverse-Media Research Agent; Risk Factor Agent; Policy Evaluation Agent; EDD Agent; Case Triage Agent; Periodic Review Agent; Monitoring Agent; Transaction-Alert Context Agent; Evidence QA Agent; Data Quality Agent; Compliance Change Agent; Security/Privacy Agent; Independent QA Agent.

No agent independently files regulatory reports, freezes assets, closes accounts or makes legally reserved compliance decisions without explicit authorized workflows.

Exact/fuzzy matching primitives; transliteration; phonetic matching; normalization; date/address parsing; registry adapters; sanctions/watchlist ingestion; list diff/versioning; ownership graph traversal; UBO threshold calculation; rule engine; risk-score calculation where formulaic; policy state machine; document hashing; audit logging; case deadlines; consent/retention; identity tokenization; encryption/key management; queue/idempotency; webhook delivery; reconciliation; export.

Identity data; identity documents; selfies/liveness results when lawful; addresses; phone/email; business formation records; registry data; tax/business identifiers; directors/officers; ownership data; corporate documents; licenses; expected activity; source-of-funds/source-of-wealth evidence where required; sanctions/PEP/watchlists; adverse-media sources; customer risk policy; transaction-monitoring alerts; account/product context; prior reviews; reviewer decisions.

## Workflow tree

Authorize customer/policy → collect identity/business inputs → normalize/tokenize → verify source evidence → resolve person/entity → build ownership graph → run deterministic screens → assess matches/confidence → gather required risk factors → execute customer/jurisdiction policy → auto-clear only explicitly authorized low-risk cases → route ambiguous/high-impact cases to compliance review → record decision/evidence → activate ongoing monitoring → trigger refresh/periodic review → ingest transaction-alert context → escalate suspicious patterns → retain/export/delete under policy.

## Integration tree

Government/business registries; identity/document providers; address/phone/email verification; biometric/liveness providers where lawful; sanctions/PEP/watchlist sources; adverse-media sources; banking/core/CRM/onboarding systems; payments; transaction monitoring; case management; SSO/identity; document storage; secure messaging; data warehouses; SIEM; regulatory reporting systems only through authorized interfaces.

## Data architecture

Tenant-isolated identity/entity/evidence stores; tokenized identifiers where possible; ownership graph; screening source registry; policy/risk-model registry; case store; monitoring event stream; audit ledger; consent/legal-basis metadata; retention; immutable decision/evidence history; encryption; region/residency; access logs; backup/recovery.

## Data moat

Potential moat: entity-resolution quality, public/licensed source normalization, ownership graph methods, screening false-positive patterns, policy/evaluation corpus, integration reliability and de-identified authorized process metrics. Never create a moat from unauthorized pooling of customer identities, biometrics or sensitive financial data.

Entity/ownership graph; source/evidence provenance; match explanation engine; risk-policy compiler; screening list versioning; false-positive reduction; case/evidence model; jurisdiction policy packs; evaluation harness; compatibility profiles.

Per verification; per business; per screen; per monitored entity; per case; subscription; API usage; enterprise license; private deployment; white-label/OEM; premium jurisdiction/source packs; case-management modules. No revenue promise.
